pages.text: Coverage Measurement Coverage Measurement Skip Navigation Within About Coverage Measurement The U.S. Census Bureau has a long history of evaluating population coverage in decennial censuses. Formal evaluations began with the 1940 census. Almost everything we know about the size of the coverage error, trends in census coverage and differences among subgroups of the population comes from the Census Bureau's own evaluation programs. Two principal methods are used to measure coverage in censuses. One method derives coverage estimates from post-enumeration surveys using dual system estimation. The other method is called Demographic Analysis (DA). DA represents a macro-level approach, where population estimates are developed for the census date by aggregating various types of demographic data. A coverage measurement program is essential for measuring the effectiveness of any census, including the 2020 Census, in terms of data quality. It is necessary to produce coverage measures to determine if the goals for 2020 were met and to determine how future censuses can be improved. This web site and its links provide an overview of these two methods, documentation of their implementation in past censuses, and documentation of their use in the 2020 Census. Demographic Analysis (DA) Demographic analysis is a technique used to develop an understanding of the age, sex, and racial composition of a population and how it has changed over time. pages.text: CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes Skip Navigation Within CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes CPS ASEC Redesign and Processing Changes April 17, 2019 Collected annually, the Current Population Survey Annual Social and Economic Supplement (CPS ASEC) is one of the most widely used socioeconomic surveys, and provides detailed information on income, work experience, poverty, health insurance coverage, and living arrangements in the U.S. In 2014, the CPS ASEC included redesigned questions on income (specifically retirement income) and health insurance coverage, followed by changes in the 2015 CPS ASEC to allow spouses and unmarried partners to specifically identify as opposite- or same-sex. While data from the updated collection methods were released on schedule, data processing changes to take advantage of this new content are now complete. This page shares information regarding these recent changes incorporated in the CPS ASEC survey design and changes to processing methods to improve data quality, and highlights the implications of these improvements for research on families and economic wellbeing in the U.S. The 2018 CPS ASEC Bridge File and the 2017 CPS ASEC Research File provide income, poverty, and health insurance estimates based on these updated CPS ASEC questions as well as a redesigned processing system. pages.title: Craig Bellamy: Wales boss takes belief from Nations League campaign - BBC Sport
pages.description: Wales finished bottom of their Nations League group, but boss Craig Bellamy believes his team showed they belong in the top flight.
pages.text: Craig Bellamy: Wales boss takes belief from Nations League campaign - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Craig Bellamy's Wales seriously tested reigning Nations League champions Portugal in Cardiff By Dafydd Pritchard BBC Sport Wales Published 17 November 2026 Craig Bellamy kept coming back to one word. Belief. His Wales side had just lost a fifth game out of six to finish bottom of their Nations League group. Bellamy would have been forgiven for feeling a little bruised. But there are ways of losing and ways of finishing bottom. Wales were fearless against Portugal, exhilarating in attack and proving they can compete at the highest level of this competition, even as they were beaten 3-2 in Cardiff. And while they were already consigned to the foot of the Group A4 table, Wales' previous performances mean they at least have the back-up of a relegation play-off in March to preserve their top-flight status. "Belief's the biggest one," Bellamy said when he was asked what he and his team had taken from this campaign. "Not just this game, but in general. We are beyond close to this level. We can more than compete at this level. "We demand and want to expect to be. Getting into League A is big for us, but also staying in A is going to allow us to develop. "You can only develop and improve by playing the best teams, and I felt we've taken another shift." IDAHO FALLS, Idaho — As Idaho Cleanup Project crews prepare used nuclear fuel for eventual shipment out of state, they are designing and building a first-of-a-kind canister handling tool considered key to success in this important project. In the Road Ready Demonstration Project, the crews will transfer the fuel from storage at the Idaho National Laboratory Site’s Irradiated Fuel Storage Facility into U.S. Department of Energy canisters. pages.description: The 2018 scandal has resurfaced this month after Usman Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about the cheating plot.
pages.text: Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Cricket Australia hopes the 'forum' will help the sport move on By Simon Atkinson and Tiffanie Turnbull Sydney Published 18 November 2026, 03:52 GMT Updated 1 hour ago Cricket Australia has launched an independent "forum" for players and staff involved in the sandpapergate scandal to share their version of events. In a memoir released earlier this month, former player Usman Khawaja claimed the entire Australia team knew of the plot to tamper with the ball during a 2018 Test in South Africa, contradicting the investigation at the time. His comments have led to a bitter split among former and current players and have overshadowed the beginning of Australia's international cricket season. The forum was not a new investigation and there will be no new penalties, Cricket Australia said, adding that nobody would be forced to take part. However, chief executive Todd Greenberg said he hoped the discussions would allow the sport to "move on". "The game is genuinely hurting at the moment. It's not good for anyone," he said. "We need to find a path through and we need some time to heal." The sandpapergate scandal is often described as one of Australian cricket's darkest days and was a source of national shame. These canyons cut through a broad, gently southwest‑tilting plateau that rises to about 6,500 feet along the area’s northeast boundary. Throughout this rugged landscape, ancestral Puebloan sites are common, adding deep cultural significance to the dramatic geologic setting. The mosaic of deep canyons that carve through the plateau - including Cross Canyon and its tributaries, Ruin Canyon and Cow Cove Canyon - reveal vivid exposures of Dakota Sandstone and the Morrison Formation. Thick stands of pinyon pine and Utah juniper cloak the uplands, while sagebrush, rabbitbrush, and cottonwood-lined canyon bottoms support wildlife ranging from deer and black bear to mountain lion, coyotes, and lizards. Cross-State Air Pollution The total pollution in any area forms from the combination of local and upwind sources. Air transport refers to pollution from upwind emission sources that impact air quality in a given location downwind. Emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO 2 ) and nitrogen oxides (NO X ) can each undergo chemical reactions in the atmosphere to form fine particle (soot) pollution. Similarly, NO X emissions can react in the atmosphere to create ground-level ozone (smog) pollution. These pollutants can travel great distances affecting air quality and public health regionally. The transport of these pollutants across state borders, referred to as interstate air pollution transport, makes it difficult for downwind states to meet health-based air quality standards for PM 2.5 and ozone. This specimen of the bird-like dinosaur Archaeopteryx exhibits what paleontologists call the dinosaur death pose or the opisthotonic death pose. Recent estimates suggest that annually about 100,000 children on the autism spectrum turn 18 in the United States. A majority of young adults on the autism spectrum have one or more co-occurring health or mental health conditions, and young adults on the autism spectrum are more likely than young adults without disabilities to be living in households with income below the federal poverty level. Young adults on the autism spectrum can face challenges to entering the labor force, including a sudden reduction of services when exiting high school (the “services cliff”). In a letter to Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander, the CCC argues that weakening the targets would result in "economic and energy security costs" and leave households "more exposed to volatile fossil fuel prices". The CCC says that switching to an electric vehicle can save a typical household around £800 a year, with fewer people benefiting if the targets were watered down. The warning comes after weeks of speculation that the government plans to announce changes to the EV targets. Government sources insist no decision has been made. Under the current rules, a "zero emission vehicle" (ZEV) mandate requires 80% of new cars sold in the UK to be zero emission by 2030 and all new cars to meet that standard by 2035. pages.text: Cyclops Myth Spurred by 'One-Eyed' Fossils? | National Geographic SCIENCE NEWS Cyclops Myth Spurred by 'One-Eyed' Fossils? New fossils fuel speculation that Greek tales may have been inspired by ancient skulls. By Hillary Mayell Published February 5, 2003 • 5 min read Ever wonder where our worst nightmares come from? For the ancient Greeks, it may have been the fossils of giant prehistoric animals. The tusk, several teeth, and some bones of a Deinotherium giganteum, which, loosely translated means really huge terrible beast, have been found on the Greek island Crete. A distant relative to today's elephants, the giant mammal stood 15 feet (4.6 meters) tall at the shoulder, and had tusks that were 4.5 feet (1.3 meters) long. It was one of the largest mammals ever to walk the face of the Earth. "This is the first finding in Crete and the south Aegean in general," said Charalampos Fassoulas, a geologist with the University of Crete's Natural History Museum. "It is also the first time that we found a whole tusk of the animal in Greece. We haven't dated the fossils yet, but the sediment where we found them is of 8 to 9 million years in age." Skulls of Deinotherium giganteum found at other sites show it to be more primitive, and the bulk a lot more vast, than today's elephant, with an extremely large nasal opening in the center of the skull. To paleontologists today, the large hole in the center of the skull suggests a pronounced trunk. Estos mosquitos prefieren picar a las personas y viven tanto adentro como afuera, cerca de las personas. Los mosquitos de la especie Aedes pueden picar de día y de noche. The BLM manages a swath of public lands along the highway from the Yukon River to the north side of the Brooks Range. Within the Dalton corridor, the BLM maintains campgrounds, rest areas, interpretive panels and the Arctic Interagency Visitor Center in Coldfoot. Similar to (and parallel to) the equator, the Arctic Circle is an imaginary line that geographers use to refer to a key characteristic of earth's rotation. It circles the northern hemisphere at a latitude of about 66½ degrees north. This latitude is important because it demarcates the southernmost boundary of a region -- the Arctic -- in which every location receives a full 24 hours of sunlight for at least one day of the year (summer solstice) and a full 24 hours without the sun rising above the horizon for at least one day of the year (winter solstice). Why 66½ degrees? Another way to think of it is 90 degrees north latitude (the North Pole) minus 23½ degrees = 66½ degrees. Okay, where does the 23½ degrees come from? Every day, the earth rotates around its axis. (The north pole marks one end of earth's axis of rotation. The south pole marks the other. The equator is halfway in between.) Dan Byers Dan Byers is Deputy Assistant Secretary (DAS) for Europe, Eurasia, Africa, and the Middle East at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of International Affairs. He is responsible for building trusted relationships to strengthen energy diplomacy and advance American interests through strategic and commercial partnerships in these regions. In this role, he leads the development and execution of regional energy strategies that expand opportunities for American energy technologies and companies while advancing broader U.S. economic and national security objectives. Prior to joining DOE, he was vice president for policy at the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Global Energy Institute, leading business community engagement and coalition building related to domestic and international energy and environmental issues.
